text:
Eh.

Wayne needed them, lol. Wayne obviously had potential, but the perception of him wasn't that good. My cousin's from Hollygrove, lived on Tchoupitoulas, is the same age, and went to school with Wayne while they were younger...he said no one had good things to say about him. When the Hot Boyz came out, people respected Juvie and B.G., thought Turk was on the come up and Wayne was kinda an extra. I heard the same things in the 7th.

Craziest thing I remember that solidified that perception was I wanna say...96 (maybe 97?) Summerjam in the Superdome. It was like...Joe, Brandy, Monica...sumone else...but the main act was No Limit (their last year), and right before them was Cash Money. Cash Money came out of a helicopter, tons of smoke everywhere, did Ha, Back That Azz Up, Bling Bling, Cash Money is a Army, then (I think) I need a hot girl....Baby gets the mic and says "we got a brand new song for y'all: never performed, no video, not on the radio, for the first time here, is my son Weezy's debut single..."Tha Block is Hot". Half of the Superdome cleared out. I was confused as fuck, so I asked my older cousin why everyone was leaving. "No Limit is the closing act and they're next, this is the last song from Cash Money, so people are getting snacks and going to the bathroom now, so they don't miss No Limit". Sure enough, everyone was back for No Limit, who came out in two hummers, shooting fireworks into the air, and obviously came out to "Make em say uhhhhhh"

Considering how he blew up afterwards, I'm always amazed by that day
